principles: Only fix real command-surface correctness drift; do not optimize unrelated code.
Prefer deletion of proven unreachable legacy surfaces over reviving unsigned or obsolete workflows.
Preserve dynamic entrypoints and regression assets unless the detector can prove they are not reachable by any supported path.
Keep Lattice workflow commands host-neutral and registered through the central registry/catalog path.
drivers: The current CLI can contain a handler implementation that users cannot call, creating false confidence.
The implementation-review legacy path lacks modern signed reviewer-run freshness semantics.
The repo uses dynamic task smoke discovery and dynamic serve modules, so naive import-graph dead-code checks would be dangerous.

options.name: A: Narrow orphan-surface detector plus high-confidence cleanup
pros: Directly catches defined-but-unregistered handler factories and command registry/catalog drift
Avoids broad dead-code optimization and keeps dynamic entrypoints safe
Matches the user instruction not to register old commands just to make code appear used
cons: Does not detect every possible unused symbol or unreachable internal helper

options.name: B: Register all orphan handlers to make them callable
pros: Would reduce orphan scan findings quickly
cons: Revives obsolete command surfaces without proving they fit modern signed review gates
Can create misleading workflow evidence and violate Lattice proof discipline

options.name: C: Broad dead-code removal using import graph
pros: Could reduce more lines of code
cons: High false-positive risk for run-all-smokes, lattice serve, init templates, and dynamic imports
Optimizes arbitrarily instead of fixing a bounded correctness issue

chosen: A: Narrow orphan-surface detector plus high-confidence cleanup
rationale: Chosen because it fixes the actual correctness failure, defined command surfaces that are unreachable, while preserving dynamic supported entrypoints and avoiding arbitrary optimization.

preMortem.scenario: Detector flags smoke tasks as orphan and blocks valid CI
preMortem.trigger: It treats package.json script references as the only task entrypoints
preMortem.consequence: Valid regression assets are removed or CI becomes noisy
preMortem.mitigation: Explicitly exempt tasks/*-smoke.ts and document run-all-smokes directory discovery semantics

preMortem.scenario: Cleanup revives old implementation_review_result commands by registering them
preMortem.trigger: The team tries to make the orphan finding disappear by adding registry entries
preMortem.consequence: Unsigned legacy review evidence can be confused with modern signed review lane evidence
preMortem.mitigation: Delete or retire the old handler instead of registering it; future migration must use review_run_start plus finding/pass commands

preMortem.scenario: Cleanup removes dynamic serve or starter support
preMortem.trigger: A static import graph misses lattice serve dynamic paths and cli-init templates
preMortem.consequence: lattice serve or generated starter projects break
preMortem.mitigation: Keep verifier/serve, devHost, bridge, browser client/server paths out of deletion scope unless a dedicated serve deprecation story proves removal safe
